s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive umbilical discomfort with a painful, ulcerated nodule and associated abdominal mass
salient_findings: Firm, ulcerated nodule at the umbilicus
Poorly defined, firm mass in the right hypochondrium
key_facts: 10-month history of umbilical discomfort
Umbilical nodule gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender
Umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm
Lesion bled on contact
Deep palpation revealed a firm mass in the right hypochondrium
Mass measured approximately 8 cm in diameter
Biopsy demonstrated well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth
CT showed irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon
Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion

s4.champion: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma

raw.champion: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a firm mass in the right hypochondrium and irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon on CT, along with a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma on biopsy of the umbilical lesion, suggests a metastatic lesion from a colorectal primary.

rejected.label: Primary umbilical adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Primary adenocarcinomas of the umbilicus are extremely rare and the presence of a mass in the right hypochondrium suggests a metastatic origin

rejected.label: Metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma to the umbilicus
rejected.why: There is no mention of gastric symptoms or findings, making this less likely

rejected.label: Metastatic small bowel adenocarcinoma to the umbilicus
rejected.why: Small bowel adenocarcinomas are rare and the findings are more consistent with a colorectal primary

rejected.label: Villous adenoma of the colon with umbilical metastasis
rejected.why: Villous adenomas are typically benign or have low-grade malignant potential, and the biopsy showed a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma
